subject: Nimbus: access gateway options for Redwood Private (VPC) - technical recommendation needed
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice@nimbuspayments.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Connecting Redwood Private to Nimbus - options and constraints

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Nimbus is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for low-latency fraud scoring in our payments path. Before we get into contracts we need a concrete recommendation for how you'd expect us to connect our production VPCs to Redwood: VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (endpoint services), or a site-to-site VPN (or a combination). A few constraints to consider:

- PCI-DSS scope: we need minimal token surface and clear auditability.
- Expected steady traffic: ~200 TPS of small JSON inference requests (peak bursts to ~800 TPS) from a single us-east-1 region; additional DR region in us-west-2.
- Latency target: tail P95 <= 60ms for the inference request+response round trip from our app tier in us-east-1.
- Customer-managed KMS for key separation; logs retained for 12 months.
- We prefer a solution that avoids sending PII over the public internet.

Can you sketch tradeoffs (latency, operational complexity, cost signals, transitive reach, private IP handling) and suggest a recommended pilot? Also any pre-reqs from us (peering account IDs, IP ranges, IAM/service principals)?

Attached: brief internal diagram showing app -> inference -> datastore (for context).

Regards,
Alice
Director, Infrastructure
Nimbus Payments

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice@nimbuspayments.com>

Subject: RE: Connecting Redwood Private to Nimbus - options and constraints

Markus / team / Alice —

Quick technical notes and a proposed hybrid pilot. TL;DR: recommend PrivateLink for control-plane and sensitive endpoints + VPC Peering for high-throughput same-region inference traffic; S2S VPN only as fallback/DR or for on-prem branches. Details below.

1) VPC Peering (same cloud provider, cross-account)
   - Latency: lowest (no NAT traversal), typically single-digit ms within region; meets P95 latency budgets when both VPCs in us-east-1.
   - Throughput: high; supports large sustained TPS without per-connection throttles.
   - Operational: simple to set up for a single region and pair of accounts.
   - Limitations: no transitive peering (can't route peered traffic through a third VPC). Requires careful CIDR planning to avoid overlap. Cross-region peering supported (but egress costs apply).
   - Security/Audit: Traffic stays inside AWS backbone; must coordinate Security Group / NACL rules and ensure flow logs are enabled for auditability.

2) AWS PrivateLink (AWS endpoint services)
   - Latency: slightly higher than peering due to proxying through ENIs and endpoint infrastructure; typical additional 3–15ms depending on payload and path — still usually acceptable for P95 but needs validation for 60ms SLA at Nimbus' tail.
   - Throughput: effective for request/response APIs; scaling handled by endpoint service (we control endpoint service on our side). Per-connection limits exist but can be scaled with parallel endpoints.
   - Operational: simpler address management (no CIDR collision) and strong security boundary: only specific ports/ENIs exposed; best for exposing discrete APIs (control plane, admin, telemetry ingestion).
   - Cost: endpoints incur hourly and data-processing charges; costs can be non-trivial at high egress volumes.
   - Security/Audit: good for minimizing blast radius; supports IAM for service-level access.

3) Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec)
   - Latency: variable; depends on internet paths and VPN concentrator. For AWS-managed S2S, traffic still traverses carrier networks — higher tail latency risk; might fail the 60ms P95 target for sensitive paths.
   - Throughput: limited by VPN throughput and tunnels; typically lower than peering. AWS has throughput caps per VPN attachment; performance can be improved with multiple tunnels/accelerators.
   - Operational: easiest for customers who cannot do cross-account peering or want on-prem connectivity; requires BGP/ASN coordination and monitoring.
   - Security/Audit: encrypted over public internet; acceptable for many workloads but may complicate PCI scoping depending on assessor interpretation.

Recommendation (Pilot topology):
- Phase A (same-region us-east-1):
  - Use VPC Peering for the inference dataplane (bulk traffic) between Nimbus app VPC and Redwood Private compute VPC. Rationale: minimal latency and predictable throughput.
  - Use AWS PrivateLink for control-plane APIs (model ops, billing, sensitive endpoints) to minimize CIDR constraints and blast radius.
  - Enable VPC Flow Logs (to an S3 bucket in Nimbus account or a cross-account logging arrangement) and route relevant logs to their SIEM for PCI audit.

- Phase B (DR / cross-region / on-prem):
  - For DR region (us-west-2), use either cross-region peering or a PrivateLink endpoint (tradeoff: peer has lower latency; PrivateLink avoids CIDR overlap).
  - Stand up a managed S2S VPN as a fallback channel for on-prem sites or branch offices that cannot use peering/privatelink.

Required inputs from Nimbus:
- Account IDs / region / primary VPC CIDR blocks (to validate peering compatibility).
- Allowed egress IP ranges (for routing and firewall rules).
- Contact for KMS/crypto key setup if they want customer-managed KMS for auditable envelope keys.
- Expected average payload size and concurrency (we have a rough TPS but need median payload bytes to estimate data transfer costs).

Attachments: reference topology and a quick cost-delta sketch (attached).

I'll produce a short runbook and an expected pilot timeline (2-week pilot) if we have the account info.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Markus / team / Alice —

Security & procurement notes:
- PCI scoping: prefer PrivateLink for control-plane and telemetry ingestion since it reduces our shared network footprint in their CDE. However, peering the inference dataplane is acceptable if we keep tokenization outside the peered path and redact sensitive fields. We should draft language stating that customer PII must be redacted before hitting non-scoped endpoints and document flow differently for assessors.
- Logging/KMS: Nimbus wants customer-managed keys. We need an appendix in the contract addressing key rotation, audit access, and incident handling.
- SLA/credits: Nimbus asked about 99.9% latency SLA for realtime inference — we should align on measurable metrics (p95 response time per region) and exclude scheduled maintenance or customer-side network issues.
- Attachments included: draft connectivity SLA and a procurement checklist.

I can share the draft SLA and a minimum-security checklist for the pilot (what we need enabled on day 0).

Kim
Dir, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Connecting Redwood Private to Nimbus - options and constraints

Alice —

Thanks for the clear brief and diagram. Based on internal analysis above, our recommendation for a pilot is:

1) Pilot topology (us-east-1):
   - VPC Peering for inference dataplane (app VPC <-> Redwood compute VPC). This keeps latency minimal and avoids per-endpoint data-processing charges.
   - AWS PrivateLink for control-plane / admin / telemetry endpoints (Redwood exposes an endpoint service; Nimbus creates interface endpoints).
   - Optional: one S2S VPN for a DR/fallback route and for any on-prem branches.

2) Security controls we will require during pilot:
   - VPC Flow Logs enabled and shared to a Nimbus S3 bucket (or cross-account CloudWatch Logs subscription) for PCI audit.
   - Customer-managed KMS for any encryption-in-flight envelope keys; we will provide a KMS integration doc.
   - Clear redaction rules documented for PII that should never traverse the inference service unless explicitly in scope.

3) Metrics & SLAs for pilot:
   - We will instrument a synthetic runner to measure P50/P95/P99 latency from Nimbus app instances to the Redwood inference endpoint over 7 days.
   - We'll target P95 <= 60ms for the inference roundtrip in us-east-1. If tails are worse, we'll iterate on instance sizing, batching, and PrivateLink endpoint count.

Next steps and ask from Nimbus:
- Share AWS Account ID(s), primary VPC CIDRs for us-east-1 and us-west-2, and an IAM contact for cross-account role setup.
- Confirm whether Nimbus wants the KMS integration in pilot or post-pilot.
- Proposed pilot week: July 19 — 23 (two-week prep window required).

Marissa will follow up to schedule the pilot kickoff and provide a test plan. Kim will circulate the draft SLA and compliance checklist. Karthik will produce the runbook and playbook for scaling endpoints if traffic spikes.

If that sounds good I can schedule a short 30-minute call with your infra lead to align details.

Cheers,
Markus
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
